name: THE NATURAL HISTORY MUSEUM
rule: VAMILY rules 416 (the big interiors: the tile stays a house), 461 (more boards), 451(a) (its ceiling at 10%), 59 (every tile its cost and its effect), 428, 441.
facts: The valley's natural history museum stands downtown by Cashman Field: halls of mounted skeletons on their plinths, habitat dioramas behind glass along the walls, display cases on the floor.

The valley's own Ice Age is at Tule Springs, north of the city: Columbian mammoths, ground sloths, camels and American lions in the old spring beds; a Columbian mammoth stood about four metres at the shoulder.
On house tiles a mounted mammoth on its plinth is a tile nobody stands on that you see through; a diorama's glass the same along the wall.
how_to_mod: A layout is 15 strings of 20 characters; every character is in 'legend'; every tile kind a legend entry names has its row in 'tiles' (its cost and its effect). A piece names the finished piece it is drawn as ('like') until this folder has its own art file (natmuseum_art.json: floor lists and a kit, the garage's format). slices/bohemia_big_inside.js lays it; slices/fight_ground/insides.json lists the insides.
districts_why: The natural history museum is its own map kind by Cashman Field: eight fights in ten there are fought inside it, by the cell's own dice; the rest at its doors and its lot.
tiles_how: Rule 59: every kind of tile says what it costs to step on and what it does. 'row' is the fight's own ground row (flat 2 AP, rough 3, height +1 a level, obstacles none); 'open' is open floor (on AUTO nobody stays on it); 'good' is ground AUTO goes to; 'say' is the one line he reads when he taps it (draft, the fewest words). [bb] each kind is a Battle Brothers ground: flat, rough, an obstacle, and cover as its trees and walls give it.

wall.effect: The museum's wall: no way through, no sight through.

floor.effect: The hall's stone floor: open ground, nothing to hide behind; on AUTO nobody stays on it.

diorama.effect: A habitat diorama behind its glass, the desert painted on its back wall: nobody passes; you see through it; cover beside it. [bb] its wall you see over.

showcase.effect: A walk-round showcase, glass on four sides: nobody passes; you see through it; cover beside it. [bb] its wall you see over.

mammoth.effect: A Columbian mammoth's skeleton on its plinth, four metres at the shoulder: nobody stands there; you see through its ribs; cover beside its plinth. [bb] its boulder.

sloth.effect: A ground sloth's skeleton reared up on its plinth: nobody stands there; cover beside it. [bb] its boulder.

case.effect: A display case, its glass starred, its fossils taken or not: cover.

benches.effect: Benches facing the skeletons: low cover.

kiosk.effect: A dead touch-screen kiosk: low cover.

bones.effect: A skeleton pulled off its plinth, bones and armature across the floor: low cover, and slow going (3 AP). [bb] its brush.
bones.say: Scattered bones: low cover, slow going.

ropes.effect: Rope stanchions round an exhibit: no cover, and slow going through them (3 AP). [bb] its rough ground.
ropes.say: Rope posts: slow going, no cover.

fire.effect: A fire somebody keeps in a trash can. It burns day and night: a man in its light is seen.
fire.say_lit: A fire: you stand in its light, and they see you.

doors.effect: The museum's doors, open: open ground, and by day the light falls in: a man here is seen.
doors.say_lit: The doors: open ground, and the day is on you.

kit_how: Every piece is drawn AS a finished piece of another kit ('like') until COOK's own picture for it is in natmuseum_art.json under the same name: then that picture is used and nothing here changes. 'kind' is what it does in the fight (COVER, LOW_COVER, WALL); 'blocks_move' means nobody stands on its tile.
start_why: NO HIGH GROUND: one floor; a plinth is a step, and its skeleton is not a place to stand.

ceiling.how: VAMILY rule 451(a): the halls' high ceiling, its track lights dead, over the board at this alpha. 'src' is the picture COOK makes; 'have' true the day it is in the folder. Until then the fight draws 'kind' itself, a stand-in (the casino's coffers).
